fault_notes: The agent never verifies the customer's identity using an account PIN, security answer, or registered address before discussing account details and troubleshooting the router. The agent otherwise investigates the repeated overnight reboots professionally, guides the customer through diagnostics, and confirms that the connection is working at the end of the call. [Label added on saving: the agent's last lines also never say "Thank you for choosing S-Net", so noclose is in this call too, though ChatGPT did not list it.]

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for calling S-Net. You're speaking with James. How can I help you today?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Hi, James. My router keeps rebooting during the night. It's happened almost every night this week, and it's getting really annoying.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I'm sorry about that. A connection dropping overnight is frustrating, especially when it keeps happening. I'll help you investigate it.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yeah, I wake up and everything's disconnected. Then I have to wait for the router to start up again before I can use anything.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That sounds disruptive. I'll check the service information and ask a few questions about the router's behaviour so we can narrow it down.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay. It usually happens sometime between one and three in the morning.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thanks, Tomasz. Does the router actually switch itself off and restart, or do you only notice that the internet connection has disappeared?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: The lights go out, then they start flashing again one after another. So it definitely looks like the whole router is restarting.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Understood. That suggests a restart rather than just a brief loss of the broadband signal. I'll check the equipment details first.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Sure. It's the router S-Net sent me when I renewed my broadband last year.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thanks. I can see the equipment information associated with your service. Let's check a few things about the power supply and where the router is positioned.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It's on a shelf in the living room, next to the television. It's been there for months.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: All right. Is the power adapter plugged directly into a wall socket, or is it connected through an extension lead or power strip?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It's plugged into an extension lead. The television and a lamp are connected to that as well.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thanks. If it's practical, we'll test the router directly from a wall socket to rule out an issue with the extension lead.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I can do that. But why would it only restart in the middle of the night? It works perfectly well during the day.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That's a good question. It could be related to power, an automatic firmware update, or an equipment fault. We shouldn't assume the cause until we check further.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I wondered about updates. Does the router install those automatically overnight?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Some router maintenance can happen automatically, depending on the model and software. I'll check whether we have any recent update information for your equipment.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, because if it's just an update, I can live with it. But this has been happening far too often.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I understand. A one-off restart can be normal, but repeated restarts every night deserve a proper investigation.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Exactly. I've got a smart heating controller and security cameras connected, and they all lose their connection when this happens.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That makes it more important to get to the bottom of it. When the router restarts, do all the indicator lights go off together?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, they all go dark briefly. Then the power light comes on, and the others follow as it starts up.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That pattern is consistent with the router rebooting. Have you noticed any unusual heat, a burning smell, or damage to the adapter or cable?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: No burning smell or damage. The router feels a little warm, but not particularly hot.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That's useful. Some warmth is normal, but make sure the vents aren't blocked and that the router has space around it for ventilation.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It's fairly close to the television, and there's a stack of magazines on the shelf underneath it. Nothing is actually covering the router, though.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I'd still recommend giving it a little more space and keeping the ventilation areas clear. We can also check the power connection and software status.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Right. Is there anything you can see from your end, or am I going to have to keep guessing?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I can check the line status and available equipment diagnostics. I'll use those results alongside what you've observed rather than leave you guessing.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Good, because I've already unplugged it and plugged it back in twice this week, and that hasn't stopped it.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thanks for telling me. Since you've already restarted it manually, there's no need to repeat that just yet. I'll check the service readings first.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: All right. I just don't want to waste another evening doing the same thing again.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I understand, Tomasz. I'll focus on the checks that can tell us something new.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thanks. Is there any chance the broadband line itself is causing the router to restart?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: A line fault can cause a connection drop, but it wouldn't usually make all the router lights go out. I'll check the line for errors anyway.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That makes sense. The lights going off completely are what made me think it was the router rather than the connection.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Your observation is helpful. The line readings look stable at the moment, and I don't see a current broadband outage affecting the service.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: So that points more towards the router or its power supply, then?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, those are possibilities worth checking. I also want to establish whether the router is running the latest available software.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I haven't logged into the router settings in ages. I wouldn't know how to check the software version.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That's fine. We can check the version through the router's administration page, if it's accessible, and I can guide you through it.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I can get to that page from my laptop. Should I open it now?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, please. Open the router settings using the address printed on its label or in the setup guide, rather than trying a random address.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I've opened it. It's asking me to sign in with the router administrator details.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Use the administrator credentials you set up for the router. Please don't read the password to me; just let me know when you're in.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I'm in now. There's a menu with status, wireless settings, maintenance, and a few other options.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Select maintenance and look for a section labelled firmware or software version. Don't press any reset option while you're there.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, I can see firmware information. There's a version number and a button to check for updates.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Please tell me the version number, but leave the update button alone until we know whether an update is available.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It says version 3.4.8. I don't remember ever seeing that before.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thanks. I'll compare that with the current version information available for this router model and see whether an update is recommended.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay. I hope this turns out to be something simple.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I hope so too. The available information indicates there's a newer firmware version for this model, so updating may help with stability.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Could that really explain why it restarts every night? Or are we just trying things at random?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: It's a reasonable possibility, but I can't promise it'll fix the issue. The update is a useful next step, and we'll monitor whether the restarts continue.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: All right, let's do it. I just want a proper solution rather than another temporary fix.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That's fair. Before you start, make sure the router stays connected to power and don't interrupt it while the update is running.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Understood. I've selected check for updates, and it's showing that an update is available.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Please follow the router's update instructions. It may restart automatically once the installation finishes, which is expected.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It's started now. The progress bar is moving, and the page says not to close the browser or disconnect the power.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That's right. Keep the power connected and let it finish. We'll wait for the router to come back online before checking the connection.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It's finished now. The lights have gone through their usual sequence, and the internet light is back on.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Excellent. Please check that your laptop can load a website, and then we'll see whether the router reports the new firmware version.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: The website is loading normally. I've gone back to the maintenance page, and the version number has changed.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Good. That confirms the update completed successfully. I'd also recommend moving the router away from the television and plugging it directly into a wall socket for the next few nights.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I can move it to the side table and use the wall socket behind the sofa. That should be easy enough.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That sounds suitable. Keep the router upright, leave space around the vents, and make sure the cable isn't stretched or loose.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Done. It's plugged into the wall now, and I've moved the magazines away so there's more room around it.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Great. We've addressed the available software update and checked the power arrangement. The important next step is to see whether the overnight restarts stop.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: So I won't know for certain until tomorrow morning, then?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That's correct. We can confirm the connection is working now, but the overnight pattern needs monitoring to establish whether the changes have resolved it.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I understand, but I'm a bit disappointed that we can't tell immediately. I've already lost sleep over this.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I understand, and I'm sorry it's been affecting your nights. I don't want to claim it's fixed before we've seen whether it stays stable.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That's fair enough. If it restarts again tonight, what should I do?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Make a note of roughly when it happens and whether all the lights go out again. Contact us if it recurs, and we can review the equipment diagnostics and arrange a replacement if indicated.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, I'll note the time if it happens. Would I need to go through all these checks again?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: No, I've recorded the troubleshooting we've completed today, including the firmware update and power-socket test. We'll use those results to decide the next step.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That's good. I don't want to have to explain the entire thing from the beginning if I call back.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Of course. The notes will help us pick up where we've left off. Is the connection still working normally for you right now?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, it's working fine. My laptop is online, and the other devices have reconnected as well.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Good, I'm glad we've restored everything for now. Just to summarise, we've updated the router firmware, moved it to a direct wall socket, and improved ventilation around it.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, that's right. I'll keep an eye on it tonight and see whether it stays on.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Perfect. Is there anything else about your broadband or router that you'd like me to check before we finish?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: No, that's everything. Hopefully I can get through a full night without the internet disappearing again.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I hope so too, Tomasz. Thanks for working through those checks with me today, and please get back in touch if the restarts continue.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thanks for your help, James. I'll see how it goes overnight. Bye.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: You're welcome, Tomasz. Have a good evening, and I hope the connection stays stable for you.
